newsitem.title: CHINA: China says building collapses partly due to graft.
newsitem.headline: China says building collapses partly due to graft.

text.p: China's construction industry is riddled with corruption resulting in shoddy quality and deadly building collapses, the official Market Daily said on Monday.
Some 27.6 percent of economic crimes in China in 1996 involved the construction industry, the newspaper said, quoting figures from the Supreme People's Procuratorate.
In the booming city of Shanghai, 39 of the 77 major bribery cases uncovered there last year involved construction firms, the newspaper said.
"Some design units and construction firms treat construction as a game and barter away licences and official stamps," it said. "They set their eyes on profits and forget what is just."
Graft was partly responsible for poor construction quality that had claimed many lives and resulted in huge economic losses through the collapse of buildings, the paper said.
"A lack of comprehensive laws and regulations has resulted in chaos in the construction market that is really cause for concern," it said.
Fierce competition, poor quality of building materials and weak supervisory mechanisms were also contributors to the industry's quality problems, it added.

About 20 people were killed and more than 40 injured when a factory dormitory in southeastern Fujian province collapsed last month. Officials said the disaster may have been caused by structural defects.
